title: Qasim Khanate
capsule: The Qasim Khanate was a Tatar vassal state on the Oka River centered at the town later called Kasimov (in modern Ryazan Oblast), established around 1452 when Grand Prince Vasily II of Moscow granted these lands to the Kazan prince Qasim, son of the Kazan khan Olug Moxammat, as a Muscovite buffer against the Khanate of Kazan. Through this dataset window (1453–1552) its khans were instruments of Muscovite policy: Qasim (r. c. 1452–1469) and his son Daniyal (r. 1469–1486) joined Moscow's campaigns against Kazan, after which rule passed to princes of the Crimean Giray line. Şahğäli (from 1515) was repeatedly installed by Moscow on the Kazan throne, and from the 1530s Russia tightened control over the khanate's internal affairs, posting a permanent representative by 1542. The Qasim khans took part in Ivan IV's decisive 1552 conquest of Kazan, the event at which this window closes.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The khanate's core territory around Kasimov is precisely attested; the extent of its effective authority at different periods is less clear and depended heavily on shifting Muscovite policy.
